pageCache.pageTitle: Hailsham Academy Careers Fair 2026 - News - Hailsham Academy
pageCache.text:
Hailsham Academy Careers Fair 2026
On Tuesday 24 March, we were delighted to welcome more than 30 local businesses, training providers, and post-16 education settings to our annual Hailsham Academy Secondary Phase Careers Fair. This event has become a highlight of our school calendar, giving every student from Year 7 to Year 11 the chance to explore future pathways and speak directly with industry professionals.
Organised by our Careers Lead, Miss Murray, the fair brings together employers, apprenticeship providers, colleges and universities under one roof. Our aim is to help students make informed decisions about their futures by offering real insight into the skills, qualifications, and career routes available to them.
Throughout the day, our students showed great enthusiasm, asking thoughtful questions, engaging positively with exhibitors, and demonstrating our MARK values. We received fantastic feedback from many of the organisations who attended, praising both the students and the smooth running of the event.
Events like this are only possible thanks to the dedication of our staff, who go above and beyond to create meaningful opportunities for our young people. We are extremely grateful to everyone involved, and we would like to extend a special thank you to all the brilliant organisations who gave their time to support the day.
“It’s been fantastic to see months of planning come together so successfully,” commented Miss Murray. “I’m incredibly proud of the event and the level of engagement from both exhibitors and students. A huge thank you to everyone involved for their enthusiasm and support. It really highlights how important careers education is for our young people.”
We are extremely proud of what our students gained from the experience and look forward to continuing to build strong partnerships with local employers and education providers, while ensuring the event continues to inspire students and support them in making informed decisions about their future pathways.
Hailsham Academy Careers Fair 2026

pageCache.pageTitle: A Level Results Day 2026 - News - Hailsham Academy
pageCache.text:
A Level Results Day 2026
Hailsham Academy students are celebrating their efforts and achievements after receiving their A Level and vocational qualification results today.
Students across Year 13 have secured places at universities, apprenticeships and employment destinations, reflecting their hard work and dedication throughout their studies.
Among those celebrating are Miriam Graham, who secured a place at the University of Oxford to study Classics and English with Latin or Greek after achieving A*, A*, A, and Molly Crosbie, who will be studying Physical Education with QTS at the University of Brighton after achieving top grades of triple Distinction*.
Jake Lambert, Head of Sixth Form, said:
"Hailsham Academy students achieve fantastic things and we are delighted to see students progressing to a wide range of exciting destinations, including university, apprenticeships and employment. With next steps ranging from journalism to accounting and from history to engineering, they will continue to produce brilliant achievements and inspire the next generation of young people here at Hailsham Academy."
Anna Robinson, Executive Headteacher, said:
"Today is a celebration of our students and everything they have accomplished. We are delighted to see them taking their next steps with confidence and ambition, and we are proud of what they have achieved during their time at Hailsham Academy. On behalf of everyone at the academy, I would like to congratulate our students on their results and thank our staff and families for the encouragement and support they have provided throughout their educational journey."
Staying Connected
All Hailsham Academy students will always be a special part of our history. By joining our free Hailsham Academy Alumni Network, our leavers can remain an important part of our future. To register, visit Alumni - Hailsham Academy and complete our online form.
A Level Results Day 2026

Hailsham Academy Students Celebrate GCSE Results
Students at Hailsham Academy are celebrating their GCSE and equivalent qualification results as they prepare for the next stage of their education, training and future careers.
These outcomes reflect the hard work, commitment and perseverance shown by students throughout their time at the academy. Whether progressing to sixth form, college, apprenticeships or employment pathways, students can be proud of everything they have achieved.
Hailsham Academy is also celebrating a number of particularly strong individual and subject successes, with students achieving excellent outcomes across a range of qualifications.
Among the highest achievers were Leonie Taylor who achieved five Grade 9s and a Distinction* at Level 2, and Exousia Usani and Hadley Manville Dobson, who both achieved excellent results including two Grade 9s. Katie Reah also achieved high results across a range of subjects.
Executive Headteacher, Anna Robinson, said:
“Our entire staff team are incredibly proud of the determination, resilience and character our Year 11 students have shown as they approached their final exams, and everything they have accomplished in their time with us. Behind every result is a student who has worked hard to overcome challenges and strive towards their goals. I would like to thank our dedicated staff, parents and carers for the encouragement, guidance and support they have provided throughout this journey. We are excited to see our students take their next steps with confidence and ambition, and we wish them every success and happiness in the future."
The academy congratulates all students receiving their results and looks forward to hearing about their future achievements.
Looking Ahead
Prospective students and families are warmly invited to attend Hailsham Academy Secondary Phase Open Day on Saturday 3 October 2026 from 9:30am to 12:30pm. Bookings for Year 6 Open Morning Tours from Monday 5 to Friday 9 October will open in September. Please visit www.hailsham-academy.org for the latest information.

pageCache.pageTitle: Year 7 Cup Final Victory - News - Hailsham Academy
pageCache.text:
Year 7 Cup Final Victory
Hailsham Academy’s Year 7 football team rounded off their season in style with a well‑earned 3–1 victory over Seaford Head in the cup final at the Peacehaven County pitch. The occasion felt special from the start, as both teams completed their warm‑ups before heading back into the changing rooms and then walking out to a crowd of around 100 supporters.
The opening stages were cagey, with both sides taking time to settle into the match and neither team fully on the front foot. Hailsham eventually found their rhythm and broke the deadlock when Louis reacted quickly inside the box, finishing confidently to give his side a 1–0 lead. Moments later came a standout moment from Emin, who scored directly from a corner to make it 2–0. It was the perfect boost heading into half‑time, and the message in the changing room was simple: keep going, stay focused, and don’t get complacent.
The second half proved much tougher as Seaford Head applied constant pressure and forced Hailsham back for long periods. Their efforts were rewarded when they pulled a goal back to make it 2–1, raising the tension among the crowd and setting up a challenging final spell. Corner after corner was defended with determination, with every player showing commitment to hold on to the lead.
Despite tired legs and rising nerves in the stands, Hailsham Academy produced the move that sealed the match. Eric played a clever pass through the Seaford defence, and Jensen finished calmly to restore the two‑goal cushion at 3–1. The team celebrated together in the corner with the bench, knowing they were close to something special. They stayed strong for the final minutes and saw the game out professionally to secure a deserved victory.
After the final whistle, each player was awarded a gold medal before the team came together to lift the South Downs Sports Partnership Cup—an unforgettable moment for the squad, their families, and the supporters who had cheered them on throughout the match. The Sheild will be on display in the sports hall trophy cabinet.
Player of the Match was awarded to Ollie for an excellent defensive performance, while Jude in goal also earned huge praise for staying composed and producing several key saves throughout the game.
Finally thank you to Ollie H who came and supported the school and the referee by volunteering his time and being linesman for the game
A brilliant end to the competition and a performance the whole school can be proud of.
Team sheet: Ollie, Emin, Jude, Lewis, Noah, Francis, Alfie, Riley, Huey, Jenson, Louis, Frankie, Jerome , Eric and assistance from Ollie H from Year 11.
During the Year 7 Assembly on Friday the team were given an awards ceremony in front of their peers, where Mr Wakeling and Mr Marsden handed them their medals and team captain Ollie was presented with the cup shield. What a great start to a Friday morning!

pageCache.pageTitle: Primary Pupils enjoy storytelling visit from Sussex author - News - Hailsham Academy
pageCache.text:
Primary Pupils enjoy storytelling visit from Sussex author
To celebrate World Book Day, pupils at Hailsham Academy Primary Phase were delighted to welcome Sussex storyteller, Helen Tozer, for a special interactive reading session arranged in partnership with Barratt Homes.
During the session, which formed part of a week of World Book Day celebrations at Hailsham Academy Primary Phase, 120 Key Stage 2 pupils listened as Helen read The Lorax and shared a series of ecology-themed folk tales. The children were encouraged to think creatively about the environment, storytelling traditions and the power of imagination.
Katie Piggott, Teaching and Learning Lead at Hailsham Academy Primary Phase, said,
“Our pupils really enjoyed the storytelling session, and it was lovely to see their excitement as the story unfolded. Workshops like this are a great way to inspire a love of reading and spark their imaginations.”
Helen Tozer also commented,
“Storytelling is a fantastic way to spark curiosity and encourage children to explore books. It was great to see how engaged the pupils were throughout the session and I hope it has kickstarted a new passion for reading.”
Barratt Homes organised the visit as part of their commitment to supporting literacy in local schools. Phil Hurring, Marketing Manager at Barratt Redrow Southern Counties, said, “Reading plays a fundamental role in the development of young children. As we create new communities at Cuckoo Fields, it’s essential that local pupils are given the chance to recognise its value and nurture a lasting love of reading.”
Throughout the week, Hailsham Academy pupils explored stories, authors and the joy of reading through a range of creative activities.

pageCache.pageTitle: Year 6 PGL Windmill Hill Residential Trip - News - Hailsham Academy
pageCache.text:
Year 6 PGL Windmill Hill Residential Trip
HOT, HOT, HOT! That was certainly the theme of our fantastic three-day residential visit to PGL Windmill Hill from 8 - 10 July. Despite the soaring temperatures, the children embraced every challenge with enthusiasm, resilience and plenty of smiles, making the trip a memorable experience for everyone involved.
Throughout the residential, pupils took part in a wide range of exciting activities that tested their courage, teamwork and problem-solving skills. Many children pushed themselves beyond their comfort zones during abseiling, showing great determination as they overcame their fears. The zipwire was another firm favourite, while Jacob’s Ladder encouraged teamwork, communication and trust. During orienteering, children demonstrated excellent navigation skills, while archery required patience and focus. Aeroball brought plenty of laughter and healthy competition, and the engaging Passport Around the World activity encouraged collaboration and fun.
Alongside the organised activities, there was also some wonderful downtime. It was lovely to see how much the children have matured, with friendships strengthening and everyone showing kindness, inclusivity and respect. Whether playing games, chatting or simply spending time together, the children represented the school beautifully and made the most of every moment.
We were also delighted to celebrate two birthdays during our stay. The birthday children were made to feel extra special as everyone enthusiastically sang “Happy Birthday” - not just once, but as many times as we could get away with! These celebrations added even more smiles and happy memories to an already fantastic trip.
The evening campfire was another highlight, bringing everyone together for songs, laughter and reflection after busy days packed with adventure. Although there was plenty of excitement and chatter in the accommodation each evening, after all the activities and fun, even the most energetic children were exhausted and eventually went to bed, ready for the next day’s adventures.
The staff were incredibly proud of how the children conducted themselves throughout the visit. Their behaviour, manners and positive attitudes were praised by the PGL instructors, and they proved to be excellent ambassadors for our school. The residential provided valuable opportunities for independence, confidence-building and personal growth, creating memories that will last for years to come.
A huge thank you to all the staff who made the trip possible, and congratulations to our amazing pupils for making PGL Windmill Hill such a tremendous success!
